problems.title: Tangent periodicity
problems.question: Simplify tan(α+3π) wherever defined.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: $\tan(\alpha+k\pi)=\tan\alpha$ for every integer k.
steps: Set k=3.

problems.title: Reduce a degree angle
problems.question: Which quadrant contains 2025°?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
steps: 225° lies strictly between 180° and 270°.

problems.title: An even function
problems.question: Which printed function is even?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: An even function satisfies $f(-x)=f(x)$. Sine is odd; cosine and squared sine are even.
steps: The expression (2sin²x+cos x)/(x²+1) has even numerator and denominator and is defined on all real x. The other choices either mix odd and even parts or are odd.

problems.title: Greatest integer below a multiple of pi
problems.question: Find the greatest integer less than 100π.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
steps: It lies between 314 and 315.

problems.title: Area of a circular segment
problems.question: A chord of length $2\sqrt2$ subtends 90° at the centre. Find the minor segment are a.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: $c=2r\sin45^\circ$ gives r=2. Segment are a is sector are a minus triangle are a.
steps: The sector are a is πr²/4=π. The triangle are a is r²sin90°/2=2.

problems.title: Simplify a radical product
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt{1+2\sin30^\circ}\sqrt{2-2\cos30^\circ}$.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: $\sin30^\circ=1/2$, $\cos30^\circ=\sqrt3/2$.
steps: The product is √(4−2√3). Since (√3−1)²=4−2√3 and √3−1>0, this is √3−1.

problems.title: Select a tangent root
problems.question: If 60°≤α≤90° and $\tan^2\alpha-(\sqrt5+1)\tan\alpha+\sqrt5=0$, find cosα.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Factor as $(\tan\alpha-1)(\tan\alpha-\sqrt5)=0$.
steps: The domain excludes 90° and the interval requires tanα≥√3. Thus tanα=√5. Then cosα=1/√(1+tan²α), positive in this quadrant.

problems.title: Range after a trigonometric identity
problems.question: Find the range of $4\sin^2x/(1+\tan^2x)+1$.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: On its domain $\cos x\ne0$, $1+\tan^2x=1/\cos^2x$. The expression is $1+4\sin^2x\cos^2x=1+\sin^22x$.
steps: Its minimum 1 is attained at x=0 and maximum 2 at x=π/4. Every intermediate value is attained.

problems.title: Cosine between vectors
problems.question: Find the cosine between (1,−1,1) and (1,1,1).
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: $\cos\theta=(a\cdot b)/(|a||b|)$.
steps: The dot product is 1−1+1=1. Both lengths are √3.

problems.title: Order points on a line
problems.question: AB=(1,−1,3), BC=(−3,3,−9). Which of A, B, C is between the others?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Let $u=\overrightarrow{AB}$. With A as origin, B=u and C=u−3u=−2u.
steps: The scalar positions are C:−2, A:0, B:1, so A is between C and B.

problems.title: Range of a rational function
problems.question: Find the range of $y=(x+3)/(x-2)$.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
steps: It never equals 1. Conversely, every y≠1 gives x=2+5/(y−1), a valid preimage.

problems.title: Triangle from graph intercepts
problems.question: Two vertices are the x-intercepts of $1/(x-2)-2$ and $\sqrt{x-2}-2$. The third is the y-intercept of $(x-2)^3-2$. Find are a.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: The first two intercepts are x=5/2 and x=6. The third is (0,−10).
steps: The horizontal base length is 6−5/2=7/2. The height is 10, so are a is (1/2)(7/2)10.

problems.title: Work rates of masters and apprentices
problems.question: Three masters complete half a job in 4 hours. Two apprentices complete the job in 18 hours. What fraction can three masters and six apprentices complete in one hour?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: The masters’ joint rate is $(1/2)/4=1/8$. Six apprentices have rate $3/18=1/6$.
steps: Add 1/8+1/6 using denominator 24.

problems.title: Two regular polygons in one circle
problems.question: A regular dodecagon inscribed in a circle has are a 12. Find the are a of an inscribed regular octagon.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
steps: For n=12,12=6r²sin30°=3r², so r²=4. For n=8, S=4·4·sin45°=8√2.

problems.title: Alternating sides of an equiangular octagon
problems.question: An equiangular octagon has alternating side lengths 1 and $2\sqrt2$. Find its are a.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Its exterior turns are 45°. Orient the length-1 sides horizontally and vertically; each slant side has horizontal and vertical projections 2.
steps: The octagon is a square of side 1+2+2=5 with four corner right isosceles triangles of legs 2 removed. Each removed triangle has are a 2. Thus S=25−8.

problems.title: Weighted alloy concentration
problems.question: Alloy masses m,2m,3m have copper content 30%,20%,10%. Find the mixed percentage.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: The copper mass is $.3m+.2(2m)+.1(3m)=m$. Total mass is 6m.
steps: The fraction is 1/6. Multiply by 100%.

problems.title: Average speed over equal distances
problems.question: A walker covers the first half of a route at 3 km/h and the second at 6 km/h. Find average speed.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
steps: For total distance d, time is d/6+d/12=d/4. Distance divided by time is 4.

problems.title: Time saved after a speed increase
problems.question: A boat increases speed by 25% after half its route and arrives .5 hour earlier. How long would the whole trip have taken at the original speed?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Let T be the original whole-trip time. The new time is $T/2+(T/2)/1.25=0.9T$.
steps: The saving .1T equals .5, giving T=5.

problems.title: Fourth trapezoid vertex
problems.question: AD is twice BC in trapezoid ABCD. A=(2,1), B=(6,5), C=(10,6). Find D.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: In the vertex order of a convex trapezoid, $\overrightarrow{AD}=2\overrightarrow{BC}$.

problems.title: Shortest vector sum
problems.question: m=(1,3), n=(a, a). For which a is |m+n| smallest?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
steps: The nonnegative squared term is zero exactly at a=−2.

problems.title: Geometric progression index
problems.question: A nonconstant geometric progression satisfies b₇b₁₂=b₂bₖ. Find k.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: For nonzero first term and ratio q, cancellation gives $q^{17}=q^k$.
steps: When |q|≠1 and q≠0, equality of these integer powers forces k=17. However, the allowed nonconstant progression with q=−1 makes the equation hold for every odd k. For example bₙ=(−1)ⁿ⁻¹ has this property.
problems.answer: Intended index: 17. Nonconstancy alone does not ensure uniqueness.
problems.note: The question needs a restriction such as positive nonconstant terms or |q|≠1 with q≠0. For q=−1, the printed odd choices 17,27,15 all satisfy the equation.

problems.title: Sum ten arithmetic terms
problems.question: aₙ=10−2n. Find the sum of its first 10 terms.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
steps: a₁=8, a₁₀=−10. Thus S₁₀=5(−2).

problems.title: Sum proper fractions
problems.question: Find the sum of all positive proper fractions with denominator 37.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: The sum is $(1+2+\cdots+36)/37$.
steps: Use 1+…+36=36·37/2 and divide by 37.

problems.title: Vector coefficients on a triangle side
problems.question: AD is a bisector and AD=αAB+βAC as vectors. Find α+β.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Since D lies on BC, $D=(1-t)B+tC$ for some t.
steps: Subtract A: AD=(1−t)AB+tAC. AB, AC are independent, so α=1−t,β=t and their sum is 1.

problems.title: An orthogonality parameter
problems.question: Unit vectors a, b are perpendicular. The vectors a+2b and 3a−kb are also perpendicular. Find positive k.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
steps: Set the dot product to zero.

problems.title: Divisors that are fifth powers
problems.question: Find the sum of divisors of $5^{55}$ which are fifth powers of natural numbers.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: The divisors are $5^j$, $0\le j\le55$. A fifth power requires $j=5k$.
steps: Sum 1+5⁵+5¹⁰+…+5⁵⁵. This is a 12-term geometric series with ratio 5⁵.

problems.title: Signs of alternating geometric terms
problems.question: b₁=−1/15, q=−1.5. Which printed inequality is false?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Even-index terms are positive and increase in magnitude; odd-index terms are negative.
steps: Thus b₄>b₅, b₄<b₆, b₁<b₄ are true. But b₈<b₁₀ because both are positive and b₁₀/b₈=q²=2.25.

problems.title: Constant sums of ten consecutive terms
problems.question: Every block of 10 consecutive terms sums to 30. If a₁₀₅+…+a₁₁₀=25, find a₁+a₂+a₃+a₄.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Subtract adjacent block sums to obtain $a_{n+10}=a_n$.
steps: The block a₁₀₁+…+a₁₁₀ sums to 30, so its first four terms sum to 30−25=5. Period 10 identifies these with a₁,…, a₄.

problems.title: An isosceles triangle from two points
problems.question: AB=BC, AC is parallel to the x-axis, A=(1,2), B=(3,8). Find its are a.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: The altitude from B to the horizontal base bisects AC. Its foot is (3,2).
steps: Thus the other base endpoint is C=(5,2), base length 4 and height 6. Area=4·6/2.

problems.title: Maximum parallelogram area
problems.question: Two altitudes from a parallelogram vertex have lengths 1,2, with angle between them in [30°,60°]. Find maximum are a.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: If θ is the acute angle between the side lines, it has the same sine as the angle between the altitude lines. Then $S=h_1h_2/\sin\theta=2/\sin\theta$.
steps: S is largest when sinθ is smallest, at θ=30°. The are a is 2/(1/2).

problems.title: Smallest term of a quadratic sequence
problems.question: Which term of aₙ=3n²−28n+2 is smallest?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: The continuous vertex is at $n=28/6=14/3$.
steps: The nearest positive integer is 5. More explicitly a₄=−62, a₅=−63, and aₙ increases as n moves farther from 14/3.

problems.title: Roots of an odd function
problems.question: An odd function on R has exactly three negative roots. How many roots has f(|x|)=0?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Oddness pairs every nonzero root r with −r and forces f(0)=0.
steps: Thus there are exactly three positive roots. For each, |x|=r gives two solutions ±r, and x=0 is one more.

problems.title: Integer-coordinate graph points
problems.question: How many points on $y=(x-4)/(x-1)$ have both coordinates integral?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: $y=1-3/(x-1)$, with integer $x\ne1$.
steps: Thus x−1 must be an integer divisor of 3:−3,−1,1,3. Each gives one distinct integer y.

problems.title: Circumference increase
problems.question: How much does a circle’s circumference increase when its radius increases by 5?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: $C=2\pi r$.
steps: The change is 2π(r+5)−2πr=10π.

problems.title: A regular octagon diagonal and side
problems.question: Find the angle between the longest diagonal of a regular octagon and a side.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: For a side sharing a vertex with a diameter diagonal, the relevant inscribed angle intercepts 3 central arcs of 45°, so it equals $3\cdot45^\circ/2$.
steps: Thus the angle between that diagonal and either adjacent side is 67.5°. If an arbitrary nonincident side is allowed, some sides instead make 22.5° with its line.
problems.note: The wording does not explicitly say the side shares a vertex with the diagonal. With unrestricted sides there are two acute line angles,22.5° and 67.5°.

problems.title: Three symmetric terms of a progression
problems.question: A 199-term arithmetic progression sums to zero. Find a₁+a₁₀₀+a₁₉₉.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
steps: The middle term is zero because the total is zero. The requested three-term sum is 3a₁₀₀.

problems.title: Diagonals avoiding the centre
problems.question: How many diagonals of a regular 16-gon do not pass through its incircle centre?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Total diagonals are $n(n-3)/2=16\cdot13/2=104$.
steps: Only the 8 opposite-vertex diameters pass through the centre. Subtract them.

problems.title: Percentage growth in an arithmetic progression
problems.question: In a positive arithmetic progression, term 3 is 20% above term 1. By what percentage is term 4 above term 2?
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Let the first term be A>0. From $A+2d=1.2A$, we get $d=0.1A$.
steps: Term 2 is 1.1A and term 4 is 1.3A. Relative growth is (1.3−1.1)/1.1=2/11. Multiply by 100%.

problems.title: Area ratios at trapezoid diagonals
problems.question: BC:AD=2:5 in trapezoid ABCD. Diagonals AC, BD meet at O, and are a COD=5. Find are a ABC.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: Similar triangles BOC and DOA give $BO:OD=BC:AD=2:5$.
steps: Triangles BOC, COD share the altitude from C to BD, so their areas have ratio BO/OD=2/5. Thus are a BOC=2. Triangles ABO, COD have equal areas: their diagonal-side products AO·BO and CO·DO are equal since AO/CO=DO/BO=5/2. Hence are a ABO=5. Add ABO+BOC.

problems.title: Graph of the maximum of two functions
problems.question: Graph $f(x)=\max(6/x,\sqrt{x-2}+1)$ on [2,∞), and find its minimum.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: $6/x$ decreases on this domain, while $\sqrt{x-2}+1$ increases. They are equal at x=3, both having value 2.
steps: Strict opposite monotonicity makes this the unique intersection. On [2,3] the maximum is 6/x; for x≥3 it is √(x−2)+1. The graph descends from (2,3) to (3,2) and then rises. Therefore its unique minimum is 2 at x=3.
problems.answer: Minimum 2 at x=3; the two graph branches are shown in the diagram.

problems.title: Longest combined work time
problems.question: Three workers take 2a,18/a,4 hours alone, where a>0. Find the maximum joint completion time and the value of a attaining it.
problems.idea: Apply the standard rule and keep the relevant domain and assumptions.
formulas: The total rate is $R=1/(2a)+a/18+1/4$. By AM–GM, $1/(2a)+a/18\ge2\sqrt{1/36}=1/3$.
steps: Thus R≥7/12 and time T=1/R≤12/7. Equality requires 1/(2a)=a/18, or a²=9. Since a>0, a=3.
